question.text: Meridian Capital (Cat II) is appointing a Merchant Banker for a new scheme launch. Which of the following appointments is PROHIBITED under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Appointing an MB that previously advised another unrelated Cat II fund
Appointing a domestic MB (vs an offshore bank)
Appointing an MB that is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the fund's Sponsor, i.e., an ASSOCIATE of the AIF's sponsor/manager/trustee
Appointing the same MB for PPM filing and ongoing annual PPM audit

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook is explicit that a merchant banker appointed by the fund shall not be an associate of the AIF, its sponsor, manager or trustee. A wholly-owned subsidiary of the Sponsor falls squarely within that associate definition, so this appointment is prohibited. The independence requirement protects the integrity of the merchant banker's role in PPM filing due-diligence certification. The Trap: Serving other unrelated AIFs is normal MB practice and does not breach independence. Domestic MBs are not only permitted but typical. The PPM-audit distractor confuses two different processes: PPM audit is carried out by an internal or external auditor or legal professional under a separate mandate, while merchant bankers provide PPM filing due-diligence certificates (including for consolidated annual intimation of PPM changes). The MB associate prohibition is independent of who conducts the PPM audit. Note: Keep the two roles distinct — the associate-bar applies to the merchant banker handling PPM filing due-diligence, while the PPM audit itself is performed by an internal or external auditor or legal professional.
